summary: Large non-software enterprises (banks, insurers, health systems, retailers, universities) hire mid/senior developers through Workday, iCIMS and Taleo pipelines where knockout questions, recruiter keyword/title filters and, increasingly, LLM-based qualification grading (Workday HiredScore, Aug 2026) decide who a human ever sees. In a defensive 2026 market where employers hold the power, these readers want a low-risk hire: someone who matches the posted title and basic qualifications, works inside Agile/SDLC and change-control discipline, ships tested integrations on cloud platforms, and understands regulated data (HIPAA, FERPA, PCI, SOX). Plain, conservative, evidence-dense résumés win; flashy design and startup self-description lose.

readers.who: ATS + knockout screen (Workday/HiredScore, iCIMS, Taleo): parsed profile, application fields and screening questions
readers.scansFor: Work authorization, location, minimum years, degree; each posted basic qualification found in parsed experience/skills (HiredScore grades A/B only if ALL basic quals are met); exact posted title and exact skill strings for recruiter Boolean searches

readers.who: Corporate/HR recruiter or talent-acquisition partner (often non-technical, high volume)
readers.scansFor: Current and previous titles, employers, dates/tenure, education; whether the title and required skills on the requisition literally appear; clean, stable work history without unexplained gaps or rapid hops

readers.who: Engineering/application development manager on the hiring team
readers.scansFor: Evidence of delivery inside an Agile/SDLC process: tested, documented integrations and APIs, CI/CD, cloud, production support, regulated-data handling, cross-team collaboration with business stakeholders, and whether gaps (e.g. Java/.NET/Azure) are learnable

readers.who: Interview panel (senior engineers, architect, sometimes business partner)
readers.scansFor: Depth behind each bullet: design trade-offs, testing strategy, how changes get approved and deployed, incident handling, communication with non-technical stakeholders

criteria.label: Meets all basic qualifications / title match
criteria.why: HiredScore grades candidates A/B only when every basic qualification is met, and Jobscan found a resume title matching the posting correlated with a 10.6x interview rate.
criteria.howToDemonstrate: Headline and summary use the posting's exact title (e.g. 'Senior Software Engineer'); each required qualification (years, degree, Agile, testing, CI/CD, APIs, cloud) is visibly evidenced in a dated job, not only in a skills list.

criteria.label: Experience in regulated environments (HIPAA, FERPA, PCI, SOX)
criteria.why: Health, finance and education postings name compliance frameworks and expect engineers to build controls into delivery, which is decisive for risk-averse employers.
criteria.howToDemonstrate: Bullets naming the framework and the control: FERPA-protected student records and SSO at Arizona State University, PCI-scoped payment flows, HIPAA/PHI handling in health-tech; one case study on access control, audit logging and data minimization.

criteria.label: Agile/Scrum delivery within the SDLC and change management
criteria.why: SOX/ITGC and university SDLC policies require authorized, tested, reviewed changes with segregated environments, so managers look for engineers who already work that way.
criteria.howToDemonstrate: Describe sprint cadence, peer code review with separation of duties, dev/test/prod promotion, release notes and change tickets; mention backlog refinement and estimation with product owners.

criteria.label: Unit, integration and end-to-end test automation
criteria.why: Automated testing is among the most-requested items in the scraped postings and is how regulated teams produce change evidence.
criteria.howToDemonstrate: Quantified bullets: test suites added (Jest unit, Playwright E2E), defects prevented, coverage of critical payment/grade-sync paths, tests gating merges in CI.

criteria.label: CI/CD pipelines and release automation
criteria.why: Enterprise postings list CI/CD tools explicitly (Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, Jenkins) and treat them as interchangeable alternatives.
criteria.howToDemonstrate: Pipeline you built in GitHub Actions: build, test, scan, deploy stages, approvals; deployment frequency or lead-time improvement; note equivalence to Azure DevOps/Jenkins pipelines.

criteria.label: APIs and system integrations with enterprise platforms
criteria.why: Non-software enterprises spend much of their engineering on connecting systems of record (CRM, LMS, ERP, payments), so integration track records map directly to the work.
criteria.howToDemonstrate: Case studies: Salesforce enrollment sync, LMS grade sync, SSO; show volumes, error handling, idempotency, reconciliation and monitoring.

criteria.label: Cloud services (AWS; Azure equivalents)
criteria.why: Postings ask for cloud resource management, monitoring, identity and databases, often accepting AWS or Azure options in the same requirement line.
criteria.howToDemonstrate: Name the AWS services used in production and, where honest, the Azure analogue in parentheses only in a skills note (e.g. 'AWS (Lambda, DynamoDB, CloudWatch); ramping on Azure'); IaC example if any.

criteria.label: Stable, progressive work history
criteria.why: 42% of employers (47% in private sector) are less likely to hire frequent job changers, and some recruiters reject 'job-hoppy' inbound candidates outright.
criteria.howToDemonstrate: Show multi-year tenure at One Origin with progression (engineer to senior/tech lead) on one dated line per role; group client engagements under the employer rather than listing them as separate jobs.

criteria.label: Collaboration with business stakeholders and cross-functional teams
criteria.why: Hiring managers rank communication/collaboration as the most-valued skill (48%) and enterprise developers serve non-technical business owners.
criteria.howToDemonstrate: Bullets on gathering requirements with university registrar/finance teams, demoing to product owners, writing runbooks for support teams.

criteria.label: Technical documentation and design artifacts
criteria.why: Missing documentation is a frequent audit failure, and secure-SDLC guidance calls for mapped architecture and data flows during design.
criteria.howToDemonstrate: Link a sanitized architecture diagram, data-flow diagram and a short design doc/ADR for one integration; mention runbooks and onboarding docs authored.

criteria.label: Production support, monitoring and incident resolution
criteria.why: Enterprise roles include on-call/production support and list monitoring tools (CloudWatch, Datadog, Splunk, Azure Monitor) among required experience.
criteria.howToDemonstrate: Bullet with an incident you resolved, a monitor/alert you added, and an uptime or error-rate outcome.

criteria.label: Industry/domain knowledge (higher ed, healthcare, payments)
criteria.why: 42% of hiring managers name industry or domain knowledge among the most-valued skills.
criteria.howToDemonstrate: Lead each role with one line of domain context (Arizona State University student platforms; health-tech patient platform) before technical bullets.

criteria.label: Bachelor's degree / certifications
criteria.why: 59.7% of recruiters filter by education and 50.6% by certifications, and a bachelor's correlated with a 6.1x interview rate.
criteria.howToDemonstrate: List 'B.S., Mathematics & Statistics' in a standard Education section; add a cloud certification (e.g. AWS or Azure fundamentals) only once earned.

redFlags.label: Missing a posted basic qualification or exact skill string
redFlags.why: Missing required skills is the top rejection reason (42%); HiredScore drops anyone lacking a basic qualification to C/D; Taleo searches don't match variants or acronyms.

redFlags.label: Heavy color, graphics, columns or text boxes
redFlags.why: 62% of hiring managers say heavy color/visual elements hurt their view of a candidate and only 13% say their ATS handles image-heavy layouts; Taleo guidance says avoid tables and graphics.

redFlags.label: Generic, AI-sounding or buzzword-heavy copy
redFlags.why: 80% of hiring managers say they can often tell AI-written resumes; giveaways include buzzwords, vague or inflated claims and repetitive wording.

redFlags.label: Frequent short stints / unclear work history
redFlags.why: Unclear or incomplete work history is a top-three rejection reason (33%), and 42% of employers hesitate to hire job hoppers.

redFlags.label: Claiming tools you haven't used to pass filters
redFlags.why: Managers report AI-tailored applications that mirror postings without real qualifications and screen harder for them; an LLM Fit & Gap view now points recruiters to the evidence behind each claim.

redFlags.label: Startup self-presentation (move fast, hustle, 'ninja', growth-hacking)
redFlags.why: Regulated employers need authorized, tested, reviewed change with segregation of duties; 'move fast and break things' framing criteria risk to them.

resume.summaryStyle: Three to four plain sentences headed by the exact target title: 'Senior Software Engineer with 6 years building and integrating web applications for higher education and healthcare...' then years, domain (regulated data: FERPA, HIPAA, PCI), core stack, and SDLC practice (Agile, automated testing, CI/CD). No adjectives about personality; one concrete outcome.
resume.bulletFormula: Past-tense action verb + what was built/changed in the posting's terms + system/stakeholder scope + process or control used (tests, review, CI/CD, compliance) + measurable outcome
resume.keywordStrategy: Mirror each posting's exact title and required-skill strings; write both spelled-out and acronym forms once (e.g. 'Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery (CI/CD)', 'Amazon Web Services (AWS)'); put skills in a plain 'Technical Skills' list AND inside dated experience bullets so parsed-profile graders find evidence; fill every Workday/iCIMS form field (skills, education, work history) since recruiters filter on fields. For missing Java/.NET/Azure/Kubernetes: do not list them as skills; show adjacent evidence (typed OO languages: TypeScript, PHP; AWS equivalents; Docker/GitHub Actions) and, if true, a short 'Currently learning: Azure' line or certification in progress.
notes: Single column, standard headings ('Professional Summary', 'Core Competencies', 'Professional Experience', 'Technical Skills', 'Education'), no tables/text boxes/icons/photo; submit text-based PDF or .docx.

Core Competencies: 9-12 keyword phrases in 2-3 short lines drawn from the requisition (Agile/Scrum, API Integration, Automated Testing, CI/CD, Cloud (AWS), Regulatory Compliance, Technical Documentation...), each one backed by an experience bullet.
Dates as Month YYYY - Month YYYY; title, employer, location on one line; group One Origin client work (ASU) under one employer entry to show tenure.
Recruiters' 6-second first pass lands on titles, employers, dates and education, so those must be instantly scannable.

ResumeGo's simulation found reviewers preferred two pages for mid-level roles (2.6x); the site's one-page format is acceptable but must not sacrifice required keywords, so cut adjectives before cutting qualifications.
Answer knockout questions truthfully: US citizen, no sponsorship needed is an asset worth stating in application fields.
Write in plain specific language; vague inflated claims and buzzwords are read as AI-generated.

portfolio.leadWith: A sober one-line positioning statement with the exact title ('Senior Software Engineer: secure integrations and web applications for regulated institutions') followed by two or three enterprise case studies (ASU SSO + LMS grade sync under FERPA; Salesforce enrollment sync; PCI-scoped payments) written as problem / constraints & compliance / approach / testing & release / outcome.
mustHave: Downloadable ATS-safe résumé (text PDF and .docx) matching the page content
Case studies that show process: requirements, design doc or diagram, test strategy, CI/CD, change approval and rollout, monitoring
Explicit compliance and data-protection notes per project (FERPA, HIPAA, PCI DSS), without disclosing confidential details
Clear dated employment timeline showing tenure and progression to senior/tech lead
Skills grouped as Languages / Frameworks / Cloud & DevOps / Data / Testing / Practices, with honest 'learning' items labelled separately
Contact details, location/remote preference, and work authorization (US citizen)
notes: Readers are not impressed by visual novelty; clarity, consistency and evidence are the trust criteria.
Frame Java/.NET/Azure/Kubernetes gaps as adjacency, not substitution: typed OO backend work, AWS services mapped to Azure equivalents, containerised CI. Never imply production use you don't have.
Metrics should be business-legible (students served, records synced, payment volume, defect or incident reduction) rather than engineering vanity metrics.
Keep AI-assisted development as a modest productivity note; hiring managers want proof through work examples rather than claims.

visual.rationale: Blue is the colour most associated with competence and trust in brand-personality research, and lower saturation reads calmer; banks, insurers and universities use navy as their institutional default, so a muted navy accent on a white page looks native to this reader. 62% of hiring managers penalise heavy colour and visual elements, so restrict colour to one accent, use a conservative serif for headings with a plain sans for labels and body, and keep a clean single-column rhythm that mirrors a traditional résumé.

interview: Recruiter phone screen confirms knockout items again (authorization, location/hybrid, salary band, years with the required stack); have a crisp honest answer for Java/.NET/Azure ('adjacent experience X, ramp plan Y').
Behavioral/competency rounds (STAR format) probe collaboration with business stakeholders, handling changing requirements, conflict, and production incidents.
Technical rounds favour practical design and code discussion over puzzles: walk through an integration end to end, API design, data modelling in SQL, error handling and testing strategy.
Expect questions on how code reaches production in a controlled environment: code review, environments, approvals, rollback, audit trail, and how you'd handle PHI/PII or cardholder data.
Panels may include an architect or business partner; explain trade-offs in plain language and connect technical decisions to risk and compliance.
